scope: Batches 001–005 only, every segment row fully read against appended original Pali. No previous judgments inspected.
prompt: data/upstream/review-rounds.md Reading prompt, with parent original-Pali-authority instruction

error_groups.rationale: English names ear/sounds on literal tongue/taste Pali. Absorb each abbreviated ear rendering into the preceding eye-plus-ellipsis span; do not equate ear with tongue.
English ear is attached to retained tongue Pali; preceding eye-feeling line includes the omitted-faculty ellipsis. Group into that preceding abbreviated span.

Mental phenomena is attached to literal tongue/tastes Pali. Previous ellipsis row contains the expanded faculty list including tastes. Group the list and mental continuation on its earliest ellipsis key; no individual mind equivalence is asserted.
Bodhi starts with face-to-face Vepacitti, the fourth Pali line, before fear/weakness and harsh words. Current subdivisions follow reordered Sujato. Group the question stanza on 2.1.
English no-one-can-reproach precedes strong-and-Dhamma-guarded, reversing these Pali lines. Group the two on 9.3.
English repaying anger precedes making oneself worse, reversing the first two Pali lines. Group on 10.1.
The people considering him a fool belongs to Jana maññanti bāloti (12.3), not attano ca parassa ca (12.2). Bodhi has already rendered self/other in 12.1. Move the distinct people clause to 12.3.
Bodhi leads with worship, which occurs on the fourth Pali line, then householders/virtue and righteous maintenance of wife. Group the complete stanza on 5.1 to avoid mapping wife to worship.
Those whom you worship precedes best-in-world in English; original Pali puts best-in-world first. Group this pair on 6.1.
English explanation/worship/king and Suja/chief attributes overlap original Pali lines 1–4 in a different order. Group the concluding stanza on 7.1.
English crossing precedes shark/demon/wave dangers; Pali names sharks/demons on 3.3 and crossing on 3.4. Group this pair on 3.3.
English puts Vulture Peak first and entirety second; Pali puts entirety first and Vulture Peak/quaking second. Group the pair on 3.1.
English Buddha-teaching, nontradition/nibbana and restraint/abandoning crosses the original first four verse lines. Group on 2.1, leaving the path lines separately.
English following teacher guidance precedes ending suffering; Pali puts ending suffering before following guidance. Group on 3.3.
English support-for-beings precedes other-world; Pali puts merit/other-world before support-for-beings. Group this pair on 3.3.
English well restrained precedes body/speech/mind; Pali names body/speech on 3.1 and mind/restraint on 3.2. Group the pair.
The first pair reverses actual-being and self-presentation; English then puts theft before the cheating gambler while Pali puts the gambler before theft. Group the four-line stanza on 2.1.
English wise discernment precedes not-practicing-what-one-says; Pali puts not-doing/speaking before wise discernment. Group this pair.
English meditators appears in 4.5 although jhāyino is on 4.6; release is on 4.5 although English puts release in 4.6. Group the pair.
English granting pardon precedes confession; original Pali confession precedes granting pardon. Group this pair.
Repeated pardon/confession pair has the same reversal of original Pali. Group on 11.1.
English ear is attached to retained tongue Pali in each repetition. Put each ear abbreviation in the preceding eye-plus-ellipsis span, leaving no false tongue equivalence.
English taught-more precedes my thoughts; original Pali my thoughts precedes taught-more. Group on 24.1.
English worship in 2.1 renders abhivande in 2.3, before dwelling/Buddha/Kokanada. Group through 2.3 on the earliest covered line, retaining the following daughter identification.
English ignorant-people/go-about on 4.1 belongs to 4.2 while noble-Dhamma on 4.2 belongs to 4.1. Group the pair.
English peace/acquiescence precedes noble Dhamma; original Pali noble Dhamma precedes peace/acquiescence. Group this pair.
English kamma-done/ignorant-person precedes greed/hatred/delusion; original Pali puts greed/hatred, delusion/ignorance, then kamma-done. Group the first three lines; retain quantity/result lines.
Bhikkhu giving rise to knowledge renders vijjaṁ uppādayaṁ bhikkhu on 14.3, not delusion/wise-person on 14.2. Move this distinct clause to 14.3; initial English sentence already covers 14.1–14.2.
English many terrors is in 5.2 but bheravā bahū occurs on 5.1. English first names creatures, then terrors/flies/serpents; group the short pair to avoid the misplaced terrors.

correspondence_concerns.rationale: Source references stand in for whole repeated passages, sometimes at a late representative key. They are not literal translations of their anchor key and are not alignment errors. Store covered Pali spans separately for eventual reveal.

English gives one thirst discourse; original rows continue into a second thirst discourse with an added English setting at 2.1 and remaining second-discourse content absent. Do not invent missing translation or miscut the first discourse.
Definitions replaced by a reference; the abbreviated volitional-formation/definition passage crosses nearby paragraph boundaries. No confidently separable misplaced meaning.
Repeated single sentences combine attention and nourishment predicates across adjacent Pali rows. These are acceptable first-key groups under Reading prompt, not errors.

Purpose formula is shared/preposed in English while the Pali repeats it through later trait/purpose permutations. Do not fabricate per-key equivalents; preserve correspondence across the shared formula and omitted permutations.

English expands intermediate faculties which original Pali abbreviates around a retained tongue representative. Where a row includes its literal tongue or mind and expanded variants, leave the valid broad rendering. Proposed grouping of SN35.63:2.7–2.8 covers an actual mental-on-tongue mismatch, without claiming a literal mind key exists in this edition.

Similes 8–12 mention the monk’s possession before its literal second Pali row, then put the benefit predicate there. This is a normal English sentence across the two rows; report no error merely for proleptic subject order.
Literal Pali misconduct and knowledge/welfare variants at 2.3–2.6 are omitted by Bodhi’s displayed source. No translated words exist to recover by moving boundaries.
Small grouped repairs preserve source order. A future correspondence layer can expose the component Pali lines within these groups without asserting monotonic individual verse matches.
